about: Shared N721NE To Do List. The web page reads and saves this file.

items.title: Vy climb gradient (ft/NM)
items.method:
At Vy (95 KIAS), near gross if practical, record VSI and GPS groundspeed at about 6,000, 8,000 and 10,000 ft MSL, plus OAT, altimeter setting, weight, wind and oil temp.
ft/NM = fpm x 60 / groundspeed. Light winds, or fly reciprocal headings and average.
Reference: Van's 1,680 fpm at 2,050 lb gross = about 1,060 ft/NM at sea level, no wind. Also note oil temp trend during a sustained Vy climb.

items.title: Autopilot engage behavior and single-axis use
items.method: In VMC, note what mode the autopilot comes up in on engage and whether it can be flown one axis only (pitch or roll).

items.title: Half flaps vs. no flaps in gusty conditions
items.method: Build experience landing N721NE with half and no flaps in gusts; note approach speeds, float, and control feel.

items.title: PMA8000BT audio panel fail-safe on COM1
items.method: On the ground, press the VOL knob (or pull the audio panel breaker) and confirm the pilot headset and mic go to COM1 (SL30), left ear only.

items.title: Emergency Power switch with master ON
items.method: On the ground, select Emergency Power with the master on. Note what the EBBS brings online and whether any display or SL30 nav steering briefly drops.

items.title: Autopilot NAV capture timing
items.method: In VMC, with the autopilot in heading mode, select NAV on an SL30 course. Note whether it starts the intercept turn immediately or waits. Decides whether to fly HDG until an ODP turn altitude before selecting NAV.

items.title: Condition inspection sign-off
items.method:
Previous condition inspection: June 26, 2024 (database).
Next one is due by the end of the 12th calendar month after sign-off: November 30, 2027 if signed off this November, December 31, 2027 if in December.

items.title: Transponder check (14 CFR 91.413)
items.method:
Last done September 3, 2024 (database log and recurring table). 24 calendar months.
Being arranged with a shop together with the pitot-static check.

items.title: Pitot-static and altimeter check (14 CFR 91.411)
items.method:
Last done September 23, 2024 (database). 24 calendar months.
Limits IFR in controlled airspace only. Being done with the transponder check.

items.title: ELT inspection (14 CFR 91.207(d))
items.method: Last done June 26, 2024 per the database. 12 calendar months. Do it in this inspection.

items.title: ELT battery: check the replacement date
items.method:
No replacement date is recorded. Read the date marked on the battery and record it.
Replace at 50% of its useful life or after 1 hour of cumulative use (14 CFR 91.207(c)).

items.title: Oil and filter change
items.due: Unknown; past 90 days if the last change was before August 21, 2026
items.method:
No oil change is logged in the database. Limit is 50 hours or 90 days.
Do the AD 2026-04-11 filter and screen check at the same time.

items.title: AD 2026-04-11 connecting rod bushings: recheck and filter/screen check
items.due: Due now if the AD applies
items.source: Due dates list, November 19, 2026; records fix list
items.method:
Recheck applicability: the AD goes by bushing part number and ship date (January 30, 2009 to September 9, 2021), not engine model. The June 28, 2024 not-affected finding used the older 2024 AD range, so check the engine ship date and rod part numbers against the AD's Table 1.
Engine S/N EL-903-80E: Lycoming's engine list shows EL-780-80E shipped September 27, 2018 and EL-914-80E shipped August 11, 2019, so this engine most likely shipped in between, inside the AD's date range (inference; confirm in the engine logbook). Strictly, a Y-prefix (non-certified) engine isn't covered by ADs, but the filter and screen check is cheap insurance.
If it applies: look at the oil filter and both oil screens for bronze particles at this oil change and every oil change after.
If it doesn't: make a not-applicable entry.

items.title: Spark plug rotation
items.method: Interval 50 hours (database). The database date of January 26, 2017 predates the engine's first start.

items.title: Propeller lubrication
items.method: Interval 100 hours (database).

items.title: Van's SB-00036 Rev 3, horizontal stabilizer rear spar cracking
items.method:
Last done August 25, 2026 at Hobbs 13.3. Interval 365 days.
Doing it during this inspection would put it on the same cycle as the condition inspection.

items.title: Record current Hobbs and tach hours
items.method:
The database's last Hobbs reading is 13.3 (August 25, 2026). Hour-based items (oil, plugs, prop lube, overhauls) can't be turned into dates without a current reading.
Also record the navigation database expiry, which isn't recorded anywhere.

items.title: Aircraft registration renewal
items.method: Issued July 11, 2023, good for 7 years (FAA registry data, third-party copy).

items.title: Engine overhaul (TBO)
items.method:
Database baseline September 30, 2024. Interval 2,600 hours or 4,380 days.
The engine is a YIO-390-EXP10 (data plate, November 23, 2026). Lycoming SI 1009BF lists 2,600 hours and 12 years for the IO-390, but says its TBOs don't apply to engines that don't match the certified configuration, so for this experimental engine the TBO is a guideline, not a limit.

items.title: Propeller overhaul (TBO)
items.method: No overhaul; the propeller went into service in 2024. No calendar limit is recorded.

items.title: Engine model: read the data plate, then fix the database
items.method:
Database says IO-390-A3B6. FAA Form 8130-6 and the POH say YIO-390-EXP10 (POH: 215 hp).
Most likely right: YIO-390-EXP10, 215 hp (inference). Read the engine data plate or Lycoming engine logbook first; note the exact suffix (EXP10 vs EXP119).
The data-plate model decides which Lycoming manuals and TBO apply.
Read November 23, 2026: data plate says YIO-390-EXP10, S/N EL-903-80E. The EXP10 is the experimental build of the 210 hp IO-390-A (the 215 hp engine is the EXP119), so use the IO-390-A manuals. Remaining: fix the Equipment row in the database.
items.result: Database Equipment row now reads Lycoming YIO-390-EXP10, S/N EL-903-80E, matching the data plate. Confirmed in the maintenance database saved November 23, 2026.

items.title: Main alternator: change AL-E160/B to AL12-EI60/B
items.method: The database's own link and the POH say AL12-EI60. Looks like a typo.

items.title: Add an equipment row for the Monkworkz MZ-30L backup alternator
items.method: No equipment row for it at all.

items.title: Oil filter: keep only the one installed (CH48110-1 or K&P S-16)
items.method: Both are listed and both are flagged for oil changes. The POH says CH48110-1. Needs your check of what's on the engine.

items.title: Transponder: make part and model agree (GTX-330 or GTX-330ES)
items.method: Part says GTX-330ES, model says GTX-330. Use whichever is installed.

items.title: Van's SB-00080 Rev 2: fix the compliance or revision date
items.source: Records fix list, November 19, 2026 (maintenance database log and SB table)
items.method: Log on February 24, 2023 says Rev 2, dated February 15, 2024. A compliance date can't come before the revision date, so one date is a typo.

items.title: AD 2001-14-51: fix the date in the log entry
items.source: Records fix list, November 19, 2026 (maintenance database log)
items.method: The log calls it dated June 29, 2021; an AD numbered 2001 is from 2001 (not checked against the AD itself).

items.title: June 28, 2024 log entry: change FAA-2024-1695 to AD 2024-21-02
items.source: Records fix list, November 19, 2026 (maintenance database log)
items.method: FAA-2024-1695 is the docket number, not the AD number. AD 2024-21-02 is now replaced by AD 2026-04-11.

items.title: AD 2026-04-11: record whether it applies and fix the interval
items.source: Records fix list, November 19, 2026 (maintenance database SB/AD table)
items.method:
Database lists it at 50 hours with no compliance recorded. The AD's interval is each oil change.
Record applicability after the ship date and rod part number check (see the inspection item).

items.title: Inspection templates: remove N459GS carry-overs; 91.414 to 91.413
items.source: Records fix list, November 19, 2026 (maintenance database recurring items)
items.method:
Carried over from N459GS: magneto timing, a stabilator, Van's SB 14-03-01 and 14-02-03, N459GS file paths, and the 2017 spark plug date.
The transponder template cites 14 CFR 91.414; the rule is 91.413.

items.title: Remove the Holley pre-filter rows
items.method: Database has a housing and element; you said there's no separate pre-filter.

items.title: Fill in blanks: Walbro pump models, flap actuator model, governor maker
items.method: Read them off the data plates.

items.title: POH section 1.1: give the full engine model
items.method: Section 1.1 says Lycoming IO-390 with no dash number. Use the data-plate model: Lycoming YIO-390-EXP10, S/N EL-903-80E, 210 hp at 2,700 RPM. Also correct any 215 hp figure in the POH to 210 hp.
items.result: POH Rev 1.11: section 1.1 engine model changed to Lycoming YIO-390-EXP10 (data plate). No logbook entry needed; no due dates changed.

items.title: POH prop: fill in blade and hub serials, add the HC- prefix
items.method: POH serials are placeholders. Model should read HC-C2YR-1BFP (the 8130-6 and database agree). Read serials off the data plates.

items.title: POH section 8.9: pumps, ECUs and coils are on fuses, not breakers
items.method: The wiring workbook shows 10 A per pump, 5 A per ECU, 15 A injector and coil.

items.title: POH oil quantity: make 7 quarts and 8 quarts agree
items.method: POH says 7 quarts maximum; its weighing section says 8 quarts in the sump. Check the dipstick marks.
items.result: POH Rev 1.11 section 1.9 now says 8 quarts maximum, which agrees with the 8 quarts in the weighing section. Listed in the POH revision record.

items.title: Main tire pressure: settle on 40 or 60 psi
items.method: POH 8.4 and 9.5 say 40 psi. The September 30, 2024 log says adjusted to 60 psi. Check Van's and the tire maker, then fix the POH or note it in the log.
items.result: POH Rev 1.11 sections 8.4 and 9.5 now say 60 PSI for the main tires, matching the September 30, 2024 log entry. Listed in the POH revision record.

items.title: POH section 8.10: drop GPS from the AHRS description
items.method: You said the AHRS doesn't use GPS.
items.result: POH Rev 1.11 section 8.10 no longer mentions GPS in the AHRS description. This change is not listed in the POH revision record.

items.title: POH section 8.8: match MZ-30L wording to how its enable is wired
items.method: POH says it's on at all times, but the MZ-30L puts out nothing unless its enable circuit is closed. If jumpered on, keep it; if switched, say so.
items.result: MZ-30L enable is jumpered, so it is always on. POH Rev 1.11 section 8.8 now says the enable circuit is jumpered closed (no cockpit switch), so it is on at all times and charges Battery 2. No logbook entry needed; no due dates changed.

items.title: POH light weight: 1,715 lb vs. 1,700 lb in the stall table
items.method: Minor. Use the weighed number.
items.result: POH Rev 1.11 uses 1,715 lb for light weight in both the performance specifications and the stall table. This change is not listed in the POH revision record.

items.title: Drawing 5A: change the 8 A backup labels to 30 A
items.source: Records fix list, November 19, 2026 (Drawing 5A, Bus Manager Power Paths)
items.method:
The MZ-30L is rated 30 A maximum (its manual): about 15 A at 900 to 1,000 RPM, 30 A at 1,800 RPM.
Redo the essential-bus load note; a fair worst case is about 15 A at idle (inference).

items.title: Drawing 5A vs. workbook: 20 A breaker on the backup side
items.method: Drawing 5A shows a 20 A breaker on the backup and BAT2 side; the workbook lists no breaker or fuse. Check the panel and fix whichever is wrong.

items.title: Workbook: B/U Alternator Enable, fill in where it goes or mark it jumpered
items.source: Records fix list, November 19, 2026 (Wiring Organization workbook)
items.method: The row sits under Panel Switches / Emergency Power Off with no terminal filled in.
items.result: The MZ-30L enable is jumpered, so there is no switch wire. The blank B/U Alternator Enable row is gone from the workbook's Function List (saved November 23, 2026).

items.title: Workbook: remove the stray Alternator (Main) from the B/U Output row
items.source: Records fix list, November 19, 2026 (Wiring Organization workbook)
items.method: Looks like a copy error.
items.result: Removed the stray Plane Power Alternator (Main) pin 1 from the B/U Alternator Output row (Function List, now row 36). The row now runs BAT2 to the B/U Alternator Reg Output Power Positive to Firewall J1 pin 1. Verified in the saved workbook. Also removed a similar stray MZ-30L pin 5 from the Roll Trim: Gnd row. No logbook entry needed; no due dates changed.

items.title: Workbook: rename TCW to EBBS
items.source: Records fix list, November 19, 2026 (Wiring Organization workbook)
items.method: About ten rows still say TCW.

items.title: FAA Form 8130-6: prop model F74792 should likely read F74972
items.method: POH, database and the Hartzell manual say F74972. Check the blade data plate, then ask your DAR or FSDO how to correct a filed form.

items.title: FAA Form 8130-6: owner name misspelled
items.method: Fix only if it matters to you.

items.title: 2024 checklist: change 210 hp to 215 hp
items.method: The earlier review also flagged its 8 quart oil figure and its gascolator mention, which you said isn't there.
items.result: No change needed. The engine is 210 hp, and the 2024 checklist already says 210 horsepower at 2,700 RPM (this item's title had it backwards).

items.title: Engine rated horsepower: confirm 210 or 215 hp before editing the POH or checklist
items.method:
Data plate confirmed YIO-390-EXP10, S/N EL-903-80E.
Lycoming's YIO-390-B manual (60297-37) rates this engine family at 210 hp at 2,700 RPM. Owner listings for other EXP10s say 210 or 215. The 215 hp figure is official for the later IO-390-EXP119.
Check the Lycoming engine logbook or factory spec sheet that came with the engine for its rated hp, then fix the POH and checklist to match.
Update November 23, 2026: the EXP10 is the experimental build of the IO-390-A (EXP10-to-EXP119 conversions are described as A3B6 to C3B6), and RV-14 listings with this engine give 210 hp. Using 210 hp; POH corrected to 210 hp in Rev 1.11. Still fix the checklist.
items.result: Rated horsepower is 210 hp (YIO-390-EXP10 = experimental IO-390-A). POH Rev 1.11 says 210 hp in all four places, with power loading 9.76 lb/hp. The 2024 checklist already said 210 hp, so it needed no change. Cruise Perf already used 210 hp IO-390-A charts. No logbook entry needed; no due dates changed.
